home.title: RetroPDF · PDF tools that never upload your files
home.description: Merge, split, rotate and edit PDFs in your browser. Your files stay on your device. No account, no limits, no uploads.
home.heading: Free PDF tools. Your files stay on your device.
home.lede: Merge, split and rotate PDFs without sending them anywhere.
home.tools_heading: Pick the tool that matches your task.
home.info.other_sites: Most free PDF websites send your document to a company’s server, change it there, and send it back. Your files end up somewhere you cannot see, and you have to trust that they are deleted.
home.info.we_differ: Here, everything runs inside your browser, on your device. Your file is never sent anywhere. That is also why there is no waiting and no daily limit: your own device does the work, not ours.
home.info.yours: Your passport, your contract, your bank statement. Whatever you are working on, it stays yours.

desktop.took_one: A number went up by one. There is no address attached to it, no account, nothing about you and nothing about this visit. It says how many, never who, and it is the only number this site keeps.
desktop.reading_one: It is one number. There is no address attached to it, no account, nothing about you and nothing about this visit. It says how many, never who, and it is the only number this site keeps.
desktop.no_email: Most sites would have asked for your email here. We did not, because this site tells you it keeps nothing, and collecting addresses on the way to that promise would make it untrue. Counting how many people were interested answers the question well enough, and it means there is nothing to leak, nothing to sell and nothing to unsubscribe from.
desktop.remembered: Your browser now remembers that you asked, so the button will say so rather than counting you twice. That is a note in your own browser and nothing is sent anywhere, the same as the two other things this site remembers.
desktop.limit: It is worth being straight about the limit of that: clearing your browser data or opening a private window would let the same person be counted again. Stopping that properly would mean keeping something about you, which is the one thing this site will not do. So the number is honest rather than exact, and it is a floor rather than a headcount.
desktop.privacy_note_after: says the same thing, and this is the number it is talking about.
desktop.would_be_1: The same tools, without a browser around them. That would mean no size limit worth mentioning, since a desktop application is not held to what a browser tab can keep in memory, and files that open straight from your computer rather than being chosen through a picker.
desktop.would_be_2: What would not change is the part that matters. It would still do the work on your own machine and still send nothing anywhere, because that is the point of the thing rather than a feature of it.
desktop.happens_1: Honestly, it depends on this number. Building and maintaining a desktop application for three operating systems is a great deal more work than a website, and it is worth doing only if people actually want it. If the count stays small, the website stays as it is, which is no bad outcome: it already does the job.
